The sweep produced no numbers because the profiling build's Metal shaders failed to compile at runtime — the C++ binary built fine, so the failure looked silent.

What was wrong: my PT_PROF patch for bit 1 ("skip mesh closest-hit") in _prof/shaders/pt_trace.metal wrote `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))` inside pt_intersect_scene, but that function has no local `params` — it reaches the parameters through the scene struct. Metal rejected the source with `program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`, and the host aborted with `metal init error: shader compile failed: ...`. Since the program compiles its shaders at startup with newLibraryWithSource (no offline metal compiler here), a bad kernel means no pipeline and no render at all, even though the .cpp/.mm compile succeeded and the binary existed on disk.

Why it printed nothing instead of an error: my sweep loop piped each run through `2>/dev/null | tail -1`, so the compile error (stderr) was thrown away and stdout had no benchmark line, leaving `PT_PROF=0 `, `PT_PROF=1 `, … with empty results; the loop's exit code was 0 because the last command was `echo`.

How I found and fixed it: I re-ran one invocation directly with stderr shown (#53-#54), saw the undeclared-identifier error, and changed the line to `scene.params->pad` (#55). No rebuild was needed because the shaders are compiled at startup, so the re-run of the same sweep printed the cost shares (full 45.35ms, no-shadow 44.05, no-mesh 4.77 → the BVH closest-hit walk is ~89% of the frame).

How I know: my own history entries #51 (the empty sweep), #53-#54 (direct run showing `shader compile failed ... use of undeclared identifier 'params'`), #55 (the fix to `scene.params->pad`) and #57-#58 (the sweep then producing numbers).
